clue.text: 20 hanks — done up by Belcher perhaps

explanation.walkthrough: A belcher is an old British name for a blue spotted neckerchief, named after the boxer Jem Belcher; the clue tempts you to think of the boxer himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty hanks of yarn make up a fixed trade measure, and a belcher (a spotted neckerchief) is the kind of cloth a traveller ties his belongings up in.

clue.text: It's wanted on return voyage down under !

definitions.text: It's wanted on return voyage down under !

parts.words: It's wanted on return voyage down under
parts.note: an Australian throwing stick is meant to make a trip out and come back to the thrower, so a return journey is exactly what it is wanted for

explanation.definitionFit: The curved Aboriginal throwing stick is designed to fly back, so it suits a homeward trip in Australia.

clue.text: Ah ! the devil-raising girl !

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the letters upwards, so the pair of pieces is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
Satan is the devil

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a girl who can raise the devil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns the whole run AHSATAN upwards, giving a Russian girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian female first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: A fairy, expert with the brogue

explanation.walkthrough: A brogue is both a stout shoe and an Irish accent; the folklore sprite is a shoemaker from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish sprite of folklore, traditionally a cobbler, so skilled with the brogue shoe while also speaking with an Irish brogue accent.

clue.text: The road to Jerusalem ?

parts.note: Bunyan's allegory follows Christian along the road to the Celestial City, the heavenly Jerusalem

explanation.definitionFit: Bunyan's allegory tells of a journey to the Celestial City, the New Jerusalem of Christian hope.

clue.text: A trimming is the making of this entrant

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are made into a new word, so this signals a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A bit of trimming turns a newcomer into a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is the making of' rearranges A TRIMMING; 'this' just points at the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person arriving to settle in a new country is an entrant to it.

clue.text: See the fish passing

explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is an instruction leading in: look at the fish, and at the phrase for passing.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spiny-finned sea fish, and a two-word phrase meaning to elapse or move past.

clue.text: Restrains some doctors

explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to confine someone, as enemy aliens in wartime; junior hospital doctors in training share the name.

clue.text: Men of the trees, relatively speaking

definitions.text: Men of the trees, relatively speaking

parts.words: Men of the trees, relatively speaking
parts.note: the trees are family trees, and relatively points to relatives: the men in them are fathers

explanation.definitionFit: Fathers and forefathers appear in a pedigree, the family tree of ancestors.

clue.text: Man of the tree, we hear, had a novel marriage

indicators.note: signals that the word for the tree is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A tree-loving man made an unusual match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had a novel marriage' points to Mrs Humphry Ward's novel 'The Marriage of William Ashe'.
explanation.definitionFit: William Ashe is the man whose marriage is the subject of a 1905 novel.

clue.text: Fall work is deeply gripping

definitions.note: an adjective phrase standing for a noun: the creature is all grip

parts.note: October is a month of the fall, the American autumn
an opus is a work

explanation.surface: An autumn piece of writing proves absorbing.
explanation.definitionFit: The eight-armed sea creature grips with its many suckers, and the word is used of any far-reaching, clutching organisation.

clue.text: Rioter in a cap ?

parts.note: a member of a mob wearing a mob-cap, the old frilled bonnet

explanation.definitionFit: A gangster is one of a mob, and a mob-cap is an old indoor bonnet, so the word suggests both.

clue.text: Faberge's coop specialities !

parts.note: Fabergé's famous jewelled creations were made for the Russian tsars each spring festival, and a coop is where hens lay

explanation.definitionFit: Fabergé's jewelled pieces were gifts for the spring festival, shaped like what hens lay.

clue.text: Girl holding an apple

explanation.walkthrough: The 'apple of the eye' is the pupil, and the coloured part of the eye encircles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, and the coloured ring of the eye, which surrounds the pupil, called the apple of the eye.

clue.text: Ne'er-do-wells summon a joker in the ship

indicators.note: the other pieces are placed inside the letters for the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
to call is to summon
a wag is a joker

explanation.surface: Rogues call for a comedian on board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Rascals and good-for-nothings, in an older spelling with a double L.

clue.text: They make a brave appearance in Paris

definitions.text: They make a brave appearance in Paris

parts.words: They make a brave appearance in Paris
parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior, and the same tribe's name was taken by Parisian street ruffians

explanation.definitionFit: A Native American people whose name was borrowed for Parisian street gangsters around 1900.

clue.text: It's wasted by many an unseen blusher

definitions.text: It's wasted by many an unseen blusher

parts.words: It's wasted by many an unseen blusher
parts.note: Gray's Elegy says full many a flower is born to blush unseen and waste its fragrance on the desert air

explanation.definitionFit: Gray's Elegy says the unseen flower wastes its pleasant fragrance on the desert air.

clue.text: Molière's misanthrope

parts.note: the hero of Molière's play Le Misanthrope, who despises the hypocrisy of society

explanation.definitionFit: He is the title character of Molière's 1666 comedy about a man who hates social pretence.

clue.text: Finally, outsize perm in seedy food-store

parts.note: an end is a finale, so finally gives the end
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lastly an oversized hairdo in a shabby grocery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' looks like it picks a last letter, but it gives a whole word; 'seedy' means in a seed, not shabby.
explanation.definitionFit: The tissue inside a plant seed that stores nourishment for the embryo.

clue.text: Significant movement described by a hand-out

definitions.text: Significant movement described by a hand-out

parts.words: Significant movement described by a hand-out
parts.note: a meaningful motion, often made by putting a hand out, rather than a leaflet

explanation.definitionFit: A meaningful movement of the body, often of the hand, to express something.

clue.text: Performer who is second to none!

parts.note: taken as written
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A performer who is the best of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second to none' usually means the best; here it is read literally as SECOND beside O.
explanation.definitionFit: In a piano duet the player taking the lower part is called the second, in Italian.

clue.text: Dial P.E.T. and get a sloth

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are got into a new order, so this signals rearrangement

parts.note: the initials are taken as letters

explanation.surface: Ring a pet and acquire a lazy animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' rearranges DIAL and PET; the word means clubfooted and is applied to the sloth, whose feet are turned in.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for clubfooted names the sloth, whose feet are bent inwards.

clue.text: Rather parti-coloured cooking utensil

parts.note: pied means of mixed colours, like a magpie
the suffix -ish means rather or somewhat

explanation.definitionFit: A deep baking dish for pastry-topped meals is kitchen equipment.

clue.text: Colour of an agile little singer!

definitions.text: Colour of an agile little singer!

parts.words: Colour of an agile little singer
parts.note: the French word for a flea, an agile little biter, names a purplish-brown shade

explanation.definitionFit: A purplish-brown shade whose name is French for flea.

clue.text: Run along and see if Dad's dressed

definitions.text: Run along and see if Dad's dressed

parts.words: Run along and see if Dad's dressed
parts.note: to dash upstairs for a quick look, with Dad called Pop and dressed meaning up and about

explanation.definitionFit: To go quickly upstairs for a short visit, as when checking whether someone is out of bed.

clue.text: Foundation-builders with a tendency to linger on the job?

definitions.text: Foundation-builders with a tendency to linger on the job?

parts.words: Foundation-builders with a tendency to linger on the job
parts.note: foundation garments are corsets, and those who build them could be read as people who stay on

explanation.definitionFit: Makers of corsets, which are foundation garments stiffened with stays.

clue.text: Pays out at the dogs ?

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: The bookmaker settles bets at the greyhound track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PAYS; at a greyhound track, 'the dogs', the dogs make sharp barks.
explanation.definitionFit: Small dogs give short shrill barks, the sound one hears at a dog track.

clue.text: Elaine the ——, Elaine the loveable " (Tennyson)

parts.note: a line from Tennyson's Idylls of the King, in Lancelot and Elaine, with one adjective missing

explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's line praises Elaine as beautiful, the adjective that completes the quotation.

clue.text: The boat could take in 50 in the peak

indicators.note: the boat could take in fifty to become the peak, so the peak is the boat with fifty added; take it away again

parts.note: a pinnacle is a peak
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A vessel could carry fifty up a mountain top.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the boat, taking in L, would become the peak, so the peak less L is the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ship's boat or light sailing vessel used as a tender.

clue.text: Burlington House boss on the line ? Nuts !

parts.note: Burlington House holds the Royal Academy, whose head is the PRA, President of the Royal Academy
taken as written

explanation.surface: The head of the Royal Academy on the phone exclaims in frustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just joins the pieces; Burlington House is the London home of the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet of nuts in boiled sugar, so nuts in a confection.

clue.text: See 4
Royal tutor impersonating Dr. Johnson

parts.note: playing a part is acting as someone
Samuel Johnson was nicknamed the Great Cham of literature

explanation.surface: A teacher of royalty does an impression of the great lexicographer.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger Ascham taught Greek and Latin to the young Elizabeth I.
